browser.description: The in-app browser's live-page windows (`browser-*`). It grants NOTHING and that is its entire content — it exists so the label is named in one place and so widening it is a visible diff rather than an accidental match of some other capability's glob. `local` is false as the belt to the braces of `remote` being absent — but note its limit: it governs plugin permissions only. The app's own `#[tauri::command]`s have no ACL manifest (build.rs defines none), and Tauri 2 checks an app command's ACL only for a remote origin, so a browsed page that ever reached an origin Tauri calls local could invoke every app command (mail_draft_send included) whatever this file says. What actually keeps `browser-*` out is the navigation gate refusing tauri:/ipc:/data:/blob: and Tauri refusing app commands from remote origins. Every defence around it is described in docs/browser_plan_b.md §2; the regression guard is src-tauri/tests/capability_scope.rs.

default.description: Tabtivity default capabilities — commands and window management. Scoped by WEBVIEW label, deliberately: per tauri-utils' own `Capability::windows` doc, a window pattern enables the capability on ALL webviews of that window regardless of `webviews`, so a `windows` glob is an over-grant the moment a window ever holds a second webview. Every window Tabtivity creates goes through `WebviewWindowBuilder`, which gives the webview the same label as the window, so this list is behaviour-identical to the old `windows` one for `main`, `detached-*` and `present-*`. There is no `remote` key here and there must never be one — a `remote` entry is the single line that would hand a browsed page the Tauri IPC bridge. `src-tauri/tests/capability_scope.rs` fails if any of that is undone.
